name: reset-indirect-entry-count
rationale: The loop-free entry ignores its grid index and unconditionally replaces the complete poisoned four-byte indirect-entry counter with aligned i32 zero.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: nan-model-sign-operations-on-nan-operands-under-fast-math
rationale: nan_signbits_fast (nan_signbits' program under the default fast math, where fabs is air.fast_fabs, -a, 0.0f - a, and -0.0f - a are one fneg fast, and saturate is air.fast_saturate) at nan_signbits' lanes: the flag state of class E (DESIGN D293). Whether Metal's sign operations keep a NaN's bits: lane i reads (a, b) and writes fabs(a) (abs is the same call), -a (fneg), copysign(a, b) and copysign(b, a) (integer operations in the AIR), 0.0f - a (an fsub), -0.0f - a (folded to the fneg, as a * -1.0f is), sign(a), and saturate(a), over nan_arith's lanes. Compiled without fast math unless named; every operand is loaded from a buffer, so nothing folds but what the AIR shows. NaN operands: quiet and signaling of either sign with payloads 0, 1, 2, 0x1000, 0x155555, 0x2aaaaa, 0x3ffffe, 0x3fffff. The output is pre-filled with 0xAB.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-five-simd-primary
rationale: One invocation calls visible-function-table slots 2 through 5 and receives exact float4 zero from all four linked _uber_clear bodies. A seven-word size table and eight explicit argument-info records keep every selector and offset in bounds; register 2 is selected. The entry writes that result to the poisoned primary texel before subgroup aggregation, and binding zero is captured byte-exactly.

name: linked-zero-work-conv2d-a20-float-int8-half
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output. Every output goes through the convolution's matrix step, whose only multiply is a 16x16x16 simdgroup matrix product, which needs Apple GPU family 10. Neither the M3 Max nor the M4 has family 10 (the Metal reference gap of the signed-off conv2d cases), so no computing variant can be qualified (TODO 6.2).
rationale: A zeroed convolution extent selects no output-channel or spatial work for one thread and retains the poisoned destination. Both direct callbacks are supplied by exact signature-compatible modules. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: reduce-two-threadgroups-of-keys-through-an-unsigned-threadgroup-max
rationale: Every key in this case has its top bit chosen so that a signed maximum and an unsigned maximum disagree, which is the whole question `air.atomic.local.max.u.i32` answers. The 8-thread grid is split into two threadgroups of four. Each group's lane 0 stores zero into the threadgroup counter, a barrier publishes it, every thread whose `tid` is below `counters[6]` -- which the buffer fixes at 6 -- folds `keys[tid]` into that counter with an unsigned atomic max, a second barrier publishes the result, and lane 0 folds the group's answer into `counters[10]` with a device unsigned atomic max. Group 0 sees 0x5, 0x80000001, 0x7FFFFFFF and 0x9, so its unsigned maximum is 0x80000001 while its signed maximum would be 0x7FFFFFFF. Group 1 sees only 0xFFFFFFFE and 0x3, because the guard drops threads 6 and 7 -- both of which hold 0xFFFFFFFF, so a guard that failed to hold would raise the final answer to 0xFFFFFFFF and say so. `counters[10]` starts at 7, which loses to both group answers, so the device max must end at 0xFFFFFFFE. The whole 2816-byte counters buffer is compared: only its bytes 2560 through 2563 may move, and the 0xCC poison in the other ten Counter slots is what shows the 256-byte stride was walked correctly. `keys` and the unused `values` buffer must both come back unchanged.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-thirty-simd-primary

name: read-and-write-a-read-write-texture-at-a-level
rationale: Sixteen threads read texel gid of a 4x4 rgba32_float read_write texture at the level lod read from constant uint buffer 0 and write 2v + 1 back at the same texel and level (texture.read and texture.write through the slot's level views, DESIGN D230). Texel (x, y) starts as (x, y, 0.5, -1); lod = 0, the texture's only level, so the result is (2x + 1, 2y + 1, 2, -1) exactly, and a read or write of another level or texel is visible. The AIR has no loop.

name: array-layer-zero-one-pixel-half-copy
rationale: One in-bounds invocation reads layer zero of the one-layer RGBA16Float array through the AIR implicit read sampler and copies the deliberate finite half4 value (1,2,3,4) to the poisoned flat output texture.

name: linear-filter-accumulator-of-rgba16-float-in-1d-and-2d
rationale: How Metal's linear filter accumulates rgba16_float texels in 1D and 2D, with float and half results: a 16x16 2D and a 16-wide 1D float texture and a 16x16 2D and a 16-wide 1D half texture, all rgba16_float, the two 2D textures holding the same values and the two 1D ones the same values. The 2D values are 64 2x2 blocks: per channel, a row (or column) of a value and its negation scaled to cancel exactly at the block's x fraction beside two smaller values with full significands; a value whose weighted term is an exact tie of the format beside a much smaller value; or, in blocks sampled at a texel centre in x, huge values in the column of weight zero beside smaller ones. The 1D values are eight pairs: a value whose weighted term is an exact tie at the pair's designed fraction, beside a much smaller value of either sign. Lane i reads a texel-space point from buffer 0: for i < 128 a 2D block at its x fraction and one of six y fractions, for i >= 128 a 1D pair at its designed fraction or another one. Each texture is sampled at the point over its size (the 1D ones at x alone) through linear clamp-to-edge and clamp-to-zero samplers with normalized coordinates; lane i writes the eight results, the half ones widened to float, to out[8i..8i+7] of buffer 1 (per texture in slot order: edge, zero), pre-filled with 0xAB. The AIR has no loop.

name: bilinear-corner-box-align-five-columns-chunk-and-remainder
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's zero-extent case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the only thread at the entry bounds check. ndArrayParams (binding 23) now holds two 80-byte entries, because the kernel reads entry MPSNDArrayRefCount - 1 = 1 for the two-entry table; entry 1's extents are (5, 3, 2, 1). The crop params (binding 29) give a 4 x 3 image with 2 channel(s) and 1 image (box index bound), scale 1.0. kMPSUserConstant = 0x1b selects bilinear resampling (kResampleMode 1), coordinate mode 3 (size box[2] - 1 = -1, origin box[0] + 0.5 = 0.5) and sampling mode 1 (scale size / (extent - 1), 0 for an extent of 1): column x samples 0.5 - x / 4 and row y samples 0.5 - y / 2, so the floor taps run from -1 to 0 and every tap is clamped into the 4 x 3 image. The grid of (4, 2, 1) threads (one threadgroup) walks columns in full 4-wide chunks plus one remainder step (x < 5), rows likewise, every depth slice and the single batch. The retained links return box coordinates 0.0, box index 0 (below the image count) and source value 1.0, so every resampled value is exactly 1.0 (all blend fractions are dyadic, so a mix of equal taps returns 1.0 in either mix form) and the observation is which columns are written: columns 0 to 4 read 1.0 and columns 5 to 7 keep the 0xab fill. The linked writer stores table entry 1 at the column coordinate, so rows and depth slices write the same column, always with 1.0: the words do not depend on write order. The destination extents bound every loop.

name: linked-zero-extent-crop-resize

name: mmul-a16-bfloat-float-float-16x16x32
rationale: Reaching variant of the zero-shape case of this entry (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero extents stop the kernel before its arithmetic. Function constant 124 (kMPSUserConstant) is 0x10842368: no transposes, A type bfloat (8), B type float (96), C type float (768), isDim16b 0, TileM = TileN = TileK = 16, SimdSx 1, SimdSy 2 (so MatProdSx 2, MatProdSy 1), edge check 0; constant 115 is 0 (no K splits, no partial reduction or partial outer tiles, no threadgroup-memory loads, no postfix linking, no z-order, no broadcast, no outer edge check, three dimensions); constant 122 is unchanged. One threadgroup of 64 lanes (2 simdgroups) runs the single 16x16 output tile with M = N = 16, K = 32 (two whole 16-deep K tiles, no remainder), B = 1. A (binding 29, bfloat) is stored [k][m] with row stride 20 elements and holds a(k, m) = ((3k + 5m + floor(km/4)) mod 9) - 4 (zero in the 4 padding columns); B (binding 28, float) is stored [n][k] with row stride 36 and holds b(n, k) = ((7n + 2k + floor(nk/3)) mod 11) - 5 (zero padding); C (binding 27, float, row stride 18) starts poisoned with 0xab. The direct path accumulates from zero with 8x8 simdgroup matrix products and stores C[n][m] = sum over k < 32 of b(n, k) a(k, m) for m, n < 16 with plain stores, so the two padding words of each C row keep 0xabababab and the 288 words observed (1152 bytes) cover the whole buffer. Every input is an integer of magnitude at most 5, exact in bfloat and float; every partial sum is an integer of magnitude at most 640, exact in float in any order or contraction. Every divisor is a nonzero constant (TileK 16, SimdSx 1, the simdgroup matrix width), the K loop runs twice, and every other loop has a constant trip count.

name: mmul-a16-bfloat-float-zero-shape
no_effect: The authored parameters give the work an empty extent, so the entry returns before any write reaches the selected output.
rationale: One thread (a 1x1 grid) with zero matrix dimensions does no matrix work and preserves the poisoned float destination. Function constant 124 (kMPSUserConstant) is 0x00400000: TileKA16 decodes to 8 and every other field is 0 (no transposes, no type selectors, no edge check; TileMA16 and TileNA16 0, SimdSx and SimdSy 1, so MatProdSx and MatProdSy 0); function constants 115 and 122 are unchanged. The parameters (binding 26, 100 bytes) are zero, so M, N, and K are 0. Every divisor on the path is nonzero: the simdgroup index by SimdSx (1) and the K extent by TileKA16 (8); every shift amount is a constant. The K extent rounded down to TileKA16 is 0, so the K loop does not run, and MatProdSx is 0, so the store loop does not run: no loop iterates and nothing is written. The direct postfix callback is supplied by its exact signature-compatible qualified module. Replaced (DESIGN D296): the linked destination callback writes table entry 1, so the case binds a two-entry table (MPSNDArrayRefSize 1 source, 1 destination) whose destination element carries the source element's fill.

name: stage-in-region-clamps-x-whatever-the-row
rationale: Two rows of four threads over a stage-in region of size 2 x 1 at origin (1, 0) (DESIGN D430): the attribute steps by thread position in grid x, so each row reads elements 1, 2, 2, 2 (origin 1 plus x clamped to the region's last element, as an M3 Max and an M4 read it, EVs SWP-stagein-m3 and -m4) and the region's height clamps nothing the x step reads: out = 0x111, 0x112, 0x112, 0x112 in both rows. Element i = 0x10 + i.

name: stage-in-region-of-size-zero-clamps-nothing
rationale: A stage-in region of size 0 at x origin 3 under four threads (DESIGN D430): the region's size less 1 wraps, so no thread is clamped and thread t reads element 3 + t, as an M3 Max and an M4 read it (EVs SWP-stagein-m3 and -m4): out = 0x113, 0x114, 0x115, 0x116. A fetch that clamped a size of 0 to element 0 or to the origin would write 0x110 or 0x113 for every thread.

name: stage-in-region-origin-adds-to-the-clamped-position
rationale: A stage-in region of size 4 at x origin 2 under eight threads (DESIGN D430): thread t reads element 2 + min(t, 3), as an M3 Max and an M4 read it (EVs SWP-stagein-m3 and -m4), so out = 0x112, 0x113, 0x114, 0x115, then 0x115 four times. Element i = 0x10 + i over ten elements, so an unclamped fetch (2 + t, to element 9) stays in bounds and writes 0x116 to 0x119 instead, and one that clamps before adding the origin writes 0x113 from thread 3 on.

name: stage-in-threads-past-the-region-read-its-last-element
rationale: A reims-vgpu consumer's shape (DESIGN D430): eight threads in one threadgroup over a stage-in region of size 6 at origin 0, stage input 0 a uint of stride 4 stepping by thread position in grid x at rate 1 (element i = 0x10 + i, eight of them so an unclamped fetch stays in bounds and reads a value of its own). Metal (the consumer's M3 Max and an M4, EVs SWP-stagein-m3 and -m4) clamps the element to the region's last, so threads 6 and 7 read element 5: out = 0x110 to 0x115, then 0x115 twice; an unclamped fetch writes 0x116 and 0x117 there. The 0xAB poison shows a dropped store.

name: one-simdgroup-of-reductions-quads-and-a-null-texture
rationale: Metal ground truth for thirteen uncovered families: air.sincos.f16 (6 case-less corpus sources), air.simd_max.f16 (3), air.simd_broadcast.s.i16 (3), air.quad_sum.v3f16 (3), air.get_null_texture_3d (3), air.simd_min.f16 (2), air.simd_min.s.i16 (2), air.simd_or.u.i8 (2), air.simd_any (2), air.simd_prefix_exclusive_sum.s.i32 (2), air.quad_sum.v2f16 (2), air.quad_sum.f16 (2) and air.sign.v4f16 (2) -- 34 sources. The dispatch is exactly one 32-thread threadgroup, which is one SIMD group here, so every reduction has one derivable answer rather than a hardware-shaped one. simd_max and simd_min put their extreme at a known lane; the signed min is negative so an unsigned comparison lands elsewhere; simd_or sees one distinct bit per lane modulo eight so all eight bits are set only if no lane was dropped; the exclusive prefix sum is i * (i - 1) / 2, different at every lane and different from the inclusive sum at all of them. quad_sum is asked at three widths and answers 16q + 6 scaled per component, which differs per quad, so a reduction that spanned the whole SIMD group lands one value for all 32 lanes. sign sees x - 3.875, which no lane makes zero, so it flips at lane 16 with no signed zero involved. is_null_texture is asked of a default-constructed texture3d and of the bound one in the same kernel, so it must answer both ways. sincos is the only inexact family; Metal and MoltenVK agree on half sin and cos, lane 0 is anchored at zero where the answers are exactly 0 and 1, and the rest were checked against a float64 derivation rounded to binary16.

name: direct-equalize-with-authored-linkage
rationale: Zero-sized linking arrays select the direct texture path while the exact visible dependencies remain authored for translation. One invocation is bounded by the authored destination extent; it samples zero texels, reads zero prefix-sum values with one authored dynamic-bin entry where applicable, and writes exact zero to every poisoned destination texel in its 1x1 or 2x2 block.

name: manual-short4-fetch-at-an-offset-transformed-onto-three-of-four-pixels
rationale: Reaching variant of this entry's manual-vertex-fetch case (TODO 6.2, WP-RVC), whose zero constants gave a degenerate position. Constant 132 enables manual fetch; table slot 0 holds the same-library callback re::vertexfetch::fetchFromShort4, and record 0 of the vertex-argument buffer (15 records of 24 bytes, the rest null) points at short4 positions with stride 8 and offset 8, which skips a leading decoy vertex (40, 40, 40). The three positions are (-1, -1), (3, -1), (-1, 3) with z = 1 (short4) with the matrix z scale 1/2, so world z = 5/8. The instance matrix (objectToCrWorld, column-major) scales x and y by 1/2, scales z and translates by (-1/4, -1/4, 1/8); crWorldToProjArray[0] keeps x, y and w and maps z to z/2 + 1/16, so the clip triangle is (-3/4, -3/4), (5/4, -3/4), (-3/4, 5/4) at w = 1. It covers the pixel centres (-1/2, 1/2), (-1/2, -1/2) and (1/2, -1/2) of the 2x2 target with a margin of at least 1/4 from every edge and misses (1/2, 1/2): pixel (1, 0) keeps its fill. The depth is the same at all three vertices, so its interpolation is exact; every product and sum is a small dyadic value, exact in float with or without contraction, and the observer writes (x + 1/2, y + 1/2, z, 1) for each covered pixel. screenSpaceDepthBias = 1/4 adds 1/4 * w to clip z: depth 0.625.

name: manual-vertex-fetch-null-buffer-defaults
no_effect: Zero instance and view constants give a degenerate position: the primitive covers no fragment, so the render target keeps its authored bytes.
rationale: Function constant 132 enables manual vertex fetch. Every zero-initialized embedded vertex-buffer pointer is null, so each AIR guard bypasses its table lookup and supplies the defined default attribute. Slot zero is the exact same-library invalid-format callback that supplies the table's required type but is unreachable. Clipping is disabled by function constant 35; its only structural backedge is capped by an unsigned 16-bit counter reaching 32. Zero transform constants produce a deterministic degenerate position. Buffer 30 and its reflected offset-zero device buffer are now authored explicitly; the invalid-format callback deterministically supplies the same default attribute when that first record is reached. This indexed AIR identity has the same reflected entry/resource/linkage contract and is authored independently.

name: average-four-samples-of-one-multisample-texel
rationale: Metal ground truth for the four uncovered multisample symbols this fragment shader is made of: air.get_num_samples_texture_2d_ms, air.get_width_texture_2d_ms, air.get_height_texture_2d_ms and air.read_texture_2d_ms.v4f32 (21 case-less sources). It is a manual MSAA resolve: it scales the incoming uv by the texture's own queried width and height, sums every sample at that texel, and divides by the queried sample count. The loop is bounded by air.get_num_samples_texture_2d_ms, and this case's texture is authored with sample_count 4, so it runs exactly four times. The harness's generated vertex stage gives the 1x1 render target's only pixel uv (0.5, 0.5), and the texture is 3 wide by 5 high, so the scaled coordinates are 1.5 and 2.5 and truncate to texel (1, 2) with half a texel of slack on either side -- no interpolation wobble can move them, and a lowering that swapped width for height would land on texel (2, 1) instead. Every other texel in the texture holds 9.0 in all four channels, so reading the wrong one cannot accidentally agree. The four samples at (1, 2) are (0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 1.0) plus 1.0, 0.5 and 0.25 respectively per sample index: every value is a small dyadic, so the four-term sum (8.0, 4.0, 2.0, 4.0) is exact under any fast-math association, and dividing by the sample count 4 gives exactly (2.0, 1.0, 0.5, 1.0).

name: linked-single-unit-decoupled-lookback-scan-max
rationale: One one-thread threadgroup processes one scan element. scanElements, elementsPerThread, threadgroups, both outer-axis lengths, all temporary-array extents, and every NDArray size and stride are one, bounding each lookback and element loop to the single dispatched lane.

name: visible-table-clear-slots-two-through-eleven-simd-primary

rationale: The clipping helper's only backedge exits at an unsigned 16-bit counter value of 32, so one fragment invocation executes at most 32 loop iterations.

name: fragment-positions-in-a-63-pixel-tile-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_position in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen: each fragment writes its [[position]] and the screen point its varyings were evaluated at (the companion's uv = (x/W, 1 - y/H) scaled by buffer 0's screen size, rounded down), into an rgba32_float target of the screen's size that holds -1 in every lane before the draw (load action); the output is the map's physical region, the texels Metal's pass rasterizes. The map is of uniform quality 0.5 on an 80x40 screen, where Apple M3's compile (DESIGN D269.1) differs from halving: 63 screen pixels to 32 physical, then the last 17 to 16, across, and the 40 rows (less than one 63-pixel tile) to 32, for a 48x32 physical image where halving gives 40x20. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region (DESIGN D269.6): two regions, 63:32 and 17:16, by one row band.

name: fragment-positions-in-a-full-quality-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_position in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen: each fragment writes its [[position]] and the screen point its varyings were evaluated at (the companion's uv = (x/W, 1 - y/H) scaled by buffer 0's screen size, rounded down), into an rgba32_float target of the screen's size that holds -1 in every lane before the draw (load action). The map is of full quality (one sample of 1.0 per axis), which Metal compiles as the identity (on Apple M3 a quality-1 map's physical size is its screen size, D265's probe), so every pixel is one fragment at its center. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region (DESIGN D269.6): the identity is one region, the whole screen, so the observation is exact.

name: fragment-positions-in-a-half-quality-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_position in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen: each fragment writes its [[position]] and the screen point its varyings were evaluated at (the companion's uv = (x/W, 1 - y/H) scaled by buffer 0's screen size, rounded down), into an rgba32_float target of the screen's size that holds -1 in every lane before the draw (load action). The map is of uniform quality 0.5 on both axes, and the output is its 16x16 corner. Apple M3 compiles it as the identity at this size: its Metal row (EV RVS-evidence) holds the identity's answer at every texel of the corner, as a 64-pixel axis at 0.5 kept its last screen pixel at one fragment per pixel after a 63-pixel tile (DESIGN D235.2, D265.2). The crate's compile is Apple's (DESIGN D269.1): the identity too, so a Vulkan candidate draws the pass as one region, the whole screen, and the observation is exact.

name: fragment-positions-in-a-quarter-quality-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_position in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen: each fragment writes its [[position]] and the screen point its varyings were evaluated at (the companion's uv = (x/W, 1 - y/H) scaled by buffer 0's screen size, rounded down), into an rgba32_float target of the screen's size that holds -1 in every lane before the draw (load action); the output is the map's physical region, the texels Metal's pass rasterizes. The map is of uniform quality 0.25 on a 128x32 screen, where Apple M3's compile (DESIGN D269.1) differs from quartering: 126 screen pixels to 32 physical, then the last 2 to 1, across, and the 32 rows to 16, for a 33x16 physical image where quartering gives 32x8. A Vulkan candidate on a device without the attachment shading rate draws the pass region by region (DESIGN D269.6, D269.7): two regions, 126:32 and 2:1, by one row band; its tiles span at least twice their physical pixels, so on a device that lists VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate the engine's candidate is the executor's typed gap.

name: fragment-positions-in-a-skewed-rate-mapped-pass
rationale: The case draws the generated fullscreen triangle (DESIGN D155) through fragment_rate_map_position in a render pass whose rasterizationRateMap is render_pass_rate_map (DESIGN D265), with the viewport the map's screen: each fragment writes its [[position]] and the screen point its varyings were evaluated at (the companion's uv = (x/W, 1 - y/H) scaled by buffer 0's screen size, rounded down), into an rgba32_float target of the screen's size that holds -1 in every lane before the draw (load action). The map is D235.8's skewed 37x23 map (horizontal 0.5 then 1.0, vertical 1.0 then 0.5), which Apple M3 compiles to a 36x23 physical image (D235.8, D265's probe); the output is that physical region, the texels Metal's pass rasterizes. A Vulkan candidate draws the pass region by region into the same 36x23 physical image (DESIGN D269.6): two regions, 33 screen pixels to 32 then 4 to 4, by one row band; the observation is exact.

name: linked-single-unit-array-multiply-nn
rationale: One invocation multiplies a 1x1 matrix pair with K equal to one. Matrix dimensions, batch counts, split counts, and NDArray extents are one; row and allocation byte strides are the exact four-byte float width, bounding every matrix and batch loop. The array declares three elements. Metal reports the third as `missing Buffer binding at index 2 for buffers.2[0]`, so every earlier observation of this case read undefined memory for it. It is authored 3.0, distinct from the 1.0 of element zero, and the written value was measured invariant under it: setting the operand pair to 2.0 and 3.0 also writes zero. This case pins the zero the linked kernel writes, not a product.

name: fragment-varying-half4-with-viewport
rationale: The fragment returns its perspective center half4 varying unchanged while structurally accepting an unused viewport index; the generated fullscreen draw captures the color byte-exactly.

name: merge-two-buffer-pointers-and-consume-the-merge
rationale: A pointer merged from two DISTINCT device buffers, consumed five ways, because Logical SPIR-V has no pointer value that can be either buffer and every consumer has to be replayed per arm. Row 0 passes the merged pointer to a `noinline` helper, which is the only shape that reaches the AIR-text inliner's pointer-select consumer path -- an ordinary helper is inlined earlier by a different rule. Row 1 indexes the merge at a runtime offset, so the access chain is taken off the select rather than off either arm. Rows 2 and 3 use a pointer PHI instead of a select: the two arms add different offsets before joining, so the frontend cannot narrow the merge, and row 3 reads the phi twice at two indices, one of them through the helper again. Row 4 merges BYTE pointers, so the word index is computed off the merge. a and b are 100..107 and 200..207 and raw is 1.0..8.0, so every row names which arm and which index it came from: an arm swap moves a value by 100, a wrong index by 1, and a lost merge writes one buffer's value on every lane instead of alternating. Odd lanes take a, even lanes take b, so both arms run in one dispatch. Every value is a small integer exact in f32 and the sums in row 3 are exact too. The last 8 floats are outside every write and pin the 0xCD fill.
